reviewed_items.reviewer_notes: Code reading is factually correct: processBlock at line 896 hardcodes Opt.none(DataColumnSidecars) instead of passing entry.columns, causing Engine API-sourced columns to bypass KZG proof verification (lines 680-695 in storeBlock). The 01e requirement (file: 01e_PARTIAL_W2B3_1771748669.json, line 733) states 'After distributed blob publishing, imported columns must behave as if received via gossip.' However, this is a SEMI-TRUSTED boundary issue per Step C2. Attacker control: none (requires compromised local EL). Path type: semi-trusted. The Engine API is JWT-authenticated and runs co-located with the CL. Exploitation requires a compromised or buggy local EL to provide malformed columns, placing the prerequisite attack outside the security model per BUG_BOUNTY_SCOPE.json trust_assumptions.engine_api. This is a correctness bug (validator may publish invalid columns if EL is faulty), not a security vulnerability exploitable by an external attacker. The bug bounty scope explicitly marks engine_api issues as conditional: 'attacks requiring a compromised local EL may be considered conditional or lower severity.'
reviewed_items.spec_reference: 01e invariant: 'forall col from EL: imported(col) => treated_as_gossip(col) == true' (PROP-6a4369e9-post-003)
